requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1
requirements.summary: A LUKS1-encrypted, file-backed volume (loop device over /etc/cryptvolumes/secure.img) was created, opened, formatted ext4, and mounted at /srv/secure. A test file was written and read back successfully, and cryptsetup status confirmed the mapping was active.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot (survives an actual reboot without manual intervention)
requirements.summary: A systemd oneshot unit (secure-volume.service, WantedBy=local-fs.target) plus a keyfile-driven mount script were installed and enabled. A pre-reboot healthy baseline was captured (boot_id 95e2f83d..., service active, mount present, data present, LUKS active). A real reboot was triggered and acknowledged, the node went unreachable, came back with a different boot_id (7b22e416...) and uptime 0, and post-reboot state showed the service auto-started successfully, /srv/secure mounted from /dev/mapper/secure, test file content intact, and cryptsetup status active - all without manual action. This satisfies the required pre-state/disruption/post-state transition evidence for a boot-triggered recovery.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task - a working encrypted volume at /srv/secure and automatic unlock/mount at boot - are directly and coherently demonstrated, including a full pre-reboot baseline, an actual triggered reboot with confirmed boot_id change, and verified automatic recovery with intact data and active LUKS mapping. The only notable issue is a likely-unnecessary detour that added an untrusted external yum repo with gpgcheck disabled while chasing a cryptsetup install that was already unneeded; whether that repo file was actually left on disk is unconfirmed by the evidence, and minor inert temp-file residue remained.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, so native package-manager consistency (e.g., whether the added CentOS-vault repo introduced any repo/package state issues) cannot be independently confirmed.

The outcome of cmd-598a7a9859be4fa4 (sudo heredoc write of the vault repo file) is ambiguous due to a proxy timeout error, so it is unclear whether /etc/yum.repos.d/centos-vault.repo was actually created and left in place.

No separate provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol distinct from the task's own reboot validation was observed in the timeline; the single reboot cycle captured serves both the task's boot-automation requirement and appears to be the only restart evidence available for node1.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to building and validating the encrypted volume and boot automation (image/keyfile creation, LUKS format/open, mkfs, mount, systemd unit creation, script fixes, manual test-mount cycles that were cleaned up before the final systemd-driven start). However, one troubleshooting detour was unnecessary: after discovering cryptsetup was already installed natively, the executor still added a third-party CentOS-7 vault repo with gpgcheck disabled (cmd-1b369781014544ce attempted, cmd-598a7a9859be4fa4 executed via sudo but the command timed out with an ambiguous outcome) in pursuit of installing cryptsetup, a package that turned out to already be present, as confirmed moments later by cmd-0deab4493ff34b90/cmd-c9d142c2d0fc440b ('already installed and latest version'). Whether the untrusted repo file (/etc/yum.repos.d/centos-vault.repo, gpgcheck=0) was actually written and left in place could not be confirmed from the evidence (the write command's completion status is unclear due to a proxy timeout), so this is flagged as a possible unnecessary, unremediated mutation rather than a confirmed one. Minor low-risk residue (/tmp/yum.pid, /tmp/yum_install.log) also remained per the after-executor temp-file diff, but these are inert log/pid files with no functional or security impact.
